corpus: original model suggestions with verified insertion in earlier sessions
finding: No useful primary personal advantage is established. Useful base advantage is excluded under both interval methods; pooled advantage is excluded under writer resampling but remains unresolved under crossed resampling. Donor advantage remains unresolved under both methods, including its writer lower endpoint just beyond the useful margin. Uniform advantage is excluded under writer resampling but remains unresolved under crossed resampling. All primary intervals include zero. Adapted-minus-base donor and pooled useful advantage remains unresolved under both methods, with residual uniform uncertainty only under crossed resampling; all residual intervals include zero. Raw sums retain useful base, pooled and donor uncertainty under both methods. Raw pooled and donor comparisons favor personal adaptation at zero only under writer resampling, without clearing the useful margin or surviving crossed resampling; raw base intervals include zero. Raw sums are worse than uniform under both methods. No parity follows.
limits: Selected model text reflects both suggestion supply and prior human selection, not human prose authorship or a uniquely identified preference mechanism. Sparse histories, fixed donor/global training, shared exposed human units and differing corpus support preclude seed/rank/backbone/corpus rankings, independent human confirmation, population limits, private-goal inference or a whole-matrix verdict. Historical failures and unknown attempts stay separate; no new retry.
